## When to apply
During any task that involves reading 3 or more files.

## Steps
1. After every 3-5 file reads, write key findings to scratchpad/notes
2. Include file paths, line numbers, and exact data - not vague summaries
3. Rewrite scratchpad sections to keep them current rather than only appending
4. Before context gets large, consolidate what you know into structured notes

## Why this matters
Context compaction can evict file contents and tool outputs at any time. If findings are only in evicted context, you must re-read files - wasting tool calls and risking different content. Notes survive compaction.

## Pitfalls
- Waiting until the end to save all findings at once - context may compact first
- Saving vague summaries instead of concrete data (paths, numbers, exact text)
- Only appending to notes without removing obsolete information
description: Save findings to scratchpad/notes every 3-5 file reads, not in one batch at the end.
